paragraphs: Friend, here's what I take from this letter. Paul is in chains, he's been deserted, and he still writes to Timothy about fire. He says, "fan into flame the gift of God," and then he adds, "For God has not given us a spirit of fear, but of power, love, and self-control." (2 Timothy 1:6-7) I run ovens all day, and a fire nobody tends goes OUT, so God's gift in you is meant to be used, not tucked away.

Now, why can Timothy be bold and not ashamed? Because it never rested on his own strength. Paul says God "has saved us and called us to a holy calling, not because of our works, but by His own purpose and by the grace He granted us in Christ Jesus before time began." (2 Timothy 1:9) Paul isn't hoping about it either. He says, "I know whom I have believed, and I am convinced that He is able to guard what I have entrusted to Him for that day." (2 Timothy 1:12)

So what do you do with that, baker? You guard the treasure you've been given, and you don't do it alone, because Paul says to do it "with the help of the Holy Spirit who dwells in us." (2 Timothy 1:14) You also stay close to the people who show up, like Onesiphorus, who was "unashamed of my chains." (2 Timothy 1:16) I bet there's someone in your life who needs a friend like that, and I bet you can be one.
